title: Nechiporenko urine test (cell count)
what: This is a test of your morning urine. It is common in Russia and nearby countries. The lab counts white cells, red cells, and casts in a set amount of urine.
why: If a routine urine test showed changes, for kidney and urinary tract problems, or to check treatment.
duration: collecting takes 5 minutes; results usually come in 1 day
tell_doctor: If you take water pills or antibiotics
If you have your period now
If you recently had a bladder scope or a catheter

prepare.title: The day before
prepare.text: Usually avoid foods that color urine, like beets and bright berries. No alcohol and no hard workouts.

prepare.title: Periods
prepare.text: The test is usually not done during your period. Move it. Ask your doctor.

prepare.title: Container
prepare.text: A sterile container from a pharmacy or the lab.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Do not stop them on your own. Tell your doctor what you take.

steps: In the morning, right after waking, wash with warm water, no soap
Pee the first few seconds into the toilet
Catch the middle part in the container
Close the container and take it to the lab within 1 to 2 hours
after: Results usually come the next day
Your doctor will explain the results

faq.q: How is this different from a routine urine test?
faq.a: It counts cells exactly in 1 mL of urine. This helps show what a routine test shows unclearly.

faq.q: Why the middle part of the stream?
faq.a: The first part washes away cells from the skin. The middle part better shows what is in your kidneys and bladder.

reminders.text: Urine cell count test tomorrow. In the morning, collect the middle part of the stream in a sterile container.
